media:group.media:title: The sound heard 3,000 miles away 🌋
media:group.media:description:
Could you sleep through a sound this loud? 👇
The 1883 eruption of Krakatoa in Indonesia made the loudest sound in recorded history. It was heard about 3,000 miles away, its pressure wave circled the planet for days, and it turned sunsets red around the world.
Sources: Nautilus ("The Sound So Loud That It Circled the Earth Four Times"), Oregon State University Volcano World ("Historical Eruption Sounds"), History.com ("Krakatoa erupts")
#Shorts #krakatoa #volcano #history #mystery #darkhistory

entry.title: What goosebumps are trying to do 🥶

media:group.media:title: What goosebumps are trying to do 🥶
media:group.media:description:
What gives you goosebumps every time? 👇
Why do we get goosebumps when we're cold, scared or hear a great song? Tiny muscles pull every hair up, a reflex left over from when our ancestors had fur.
Sources: BrainFacts.org / Society for Neuroscience ("What Causes Goosebumps?"), Harvard Stem Cell Institute (Shwartz et al., Cell, July 2020), Science News
#Shorts #goosebumps #humanbody #science #facts

entry.title: What if the dinosaur asteroid hit today? ☄️

media:group.media:title: What if the dinosaur asteroid hit today? ☄️
media:group.media:description:
Where would you hide if it hit tomorrow? 👇
What would happen if the Chicxulub asteroid that wiped out the dinosaurs hit Earth today? A mile-high tsunami, a sky that rains hot rock, and years without sunlight. Some details, like global wildfires, are still debated by scientists.
Sources: AGU (Range et al. 2022, AGU Advances, global tsunami simulation with NOAA PMEL & University of Michigan), AGU press release on Purdue study, J. Geophys. Res. Biogeosciences (July 2026), Smithsonian Magazine
#Shorts #asteroid #dinosaurs #space #whatif #science #facts

entry.title: The town that's been burning since 1962 🔥

media:group.media:title: The town that's been burning since 1962 🔥
media:group.media:description:
Would you visit a town that's still on fire? 👇
Centralia, Pennsylvania has had a coal mine fire burning under it since 1962. It turned a mining town into a near ghost town.
Sources: Pennsylvania DEP ("Centralia Mine Fire Resources"), History.com ("This Mine Fire Has Been Burning for More Than 50 Years")
#Shorts #centralia #ghosttown #darkhistory #history #mystery

media:group.media:title: Why you can't tickle yourself 🪶
media:group.media:description:
Are you the most ticklish person you know? 👇
Why can't you tickle yourself? Your brain predicts your own touch and turns it down, and a 1999 robot experiment found a way around it.
Sources: Blakemore, Wolpert & Frith, Nature Neuroscience (1998) "Central cancellation of self-produced tickle sensation", Blakemore, Frith & Wolpert, Journal of Cognitive Neuroscience (1999) "Spatio-temporal prediction modulates the perception of self-produced stimuli", UCL News ("Why can't I tickle myself?")
#Shorts #brain #tickle #psychology #facts

media:group.media:title: What if Yellowstone erupted tonight? 🌋
media:group.media:description:
Would ash reach your city? 👇
What would happen if the Yellowstone supervolcano erupted? A USGS model shows ash falling across all of North America, from a meter near the park to millimeters on the coasts.
Sources: USGS ("What would happen if a supervolcano eruption occurred again at Yellowstone?"), Mastin et al., Geochemistry, Geophysics, Geosystems (2014) via AGU ("Yellowstone supereruption would send ash across North America")
#Shorts #yellowstone #volcano #supervolcano #whatif #science #facts

entry.title: America's deadliest fire that nobody remembers 🔥

media:group.media:title: America's deadliest fire that nobody remembers 🔥
media:group.media:description:
Had you ever heard of this fire? 👇
The Peshtigo Fire of October 8, 1871 is the deadliest wildfire in US history, yet it was overshadowed by the Great Chicago Fire on the very same night.
Sources: NOAA National Weather Service Green Bay ("The Peshtigo Fire"), Wisconsin Historical Society marker "Peshtigo Fire Cemetery" (HMdb), University of Wisconsin WI101 ("Two Fires"), Earth Magazine ("October 8, 1871: The deadliest wildfire in American history")
#Shorts #peshtigofire #history #wildfire #mystery #darkhistory

entry.title: Why IKEA makes you build it yourself 🔧

media:group.media:title: Why IKEA makes you build it yourself 🔧
media:group.media:description:
Do you love the furniture you built yourself? 👇
Why does IKEA sell flat-pack furniture you have to assemble? It started with a table that wouldn't fit in a car, and it pays off twice: lower costs and the IKEA effect.
Sources: IKEA Museum ("Flatpacks"), Dezeen ("IKEA relaunches first flat-pack table", 2013), Wallpaper ("Ikea leaf table"), Norton, Mochon & Ariely, Journal of Consumer Psychology (2012) "The IKEA effect: When labor leads to love"
#Shorts #ikea #business #ikeaeffect #entrepreneur #history

entry.title: What if the Moon vanished tonight? 🌑

media:group.media:title: What if the Moon vanished tonight? 🌑
media:group.media:description:
What would you miss first? 👇
What would happen to Earth if the Moon disappeared? Darker nights and weaker tides come first, but the biggest change is the slowest one: Earth's tilt.
Sources: Ocean Motion / NASA ("Tide-Generating Forces"), Australian Institute of Marine Science via The Conversation ("Mass coral spawning"), Laskar, Joutel & Robutel, Nature (1993), Li & Batygin, ApJ (2014) "On the Spin-axis Dynamics of a Moonless Earth", Live Science ("What would happen if the moon disappeared?")
#Shorts #moon #space #earth #whatif #science #facts

media:group.media:title: The year summer never came ❄️
media:group.media:description:
Would you have guessed a volcano? 👇
In 1816, the Year Without a Summer, snow fell in New England in June and harvests failed across Europe. The cause was the 1815 eruption of Mount Tambora in Indonesia.
Sources: Smithsonian Magazine ("Blast from the Past"), UCAR Center for Science Education ("Mount Tambora and the Year Without a Summer")
#Shorts #history #volcano #darkhistory #mystery

entry.title: Why your body jolts just as you fall asleep ⚡

media:group.media:title: Why your body jolts just as you fall asleep ⚡
media:group.media:description:
Does this happen to you every night? 👇
That sudden jolt or falling feeling as you drift off is called a hypnic jerk. Up to 70% of people get them, and scientists still debate why.
Sources: Oswald, Brain (1959) "Sudden bodily jerks on falling asleep", McGill Office for Science and Society ("What are Hypnic Jerks"), Sleep Foundation ("Hypnic Jerks")
#Shorts #sleep #brain #hypnicjerk #psychology #facts

entry.title: What if the 1859 solar storm hit today? ☀️

media:group.media:title: What if the 1859 solar storm hit today? ☀️
media:group.media:description:
Would your town keep the lights on? 👇
What would happen if a Carrington Event solar storm like 1859 hit Earth today? Power grids, satellites and GPS are at risk, and in 2012 a storm that strong missed us by about a week.
Sources: NASA Science ("Near Miss: The Solar Superstorm of July 2012"), USGS ("What a Solar Superstorm Could Mean for the US"), National Academy of Sciences report (2008) via NASA, Riley, Space Weather (2012) via NASA
#Shorts #solarstorm #sun #space #whatif #science #facts

entry.title: The women who glowed in the dark ☢️

media:group.media:title: The women who glowed in the dark ☢️
media:group.media:description:
Did you know their story before today? 👇
The Radium Girls painted glowing watch dials in the 1910s and 1920s and were told the paint was safe. Their fight changed worker safety forever.
Sources: Science Museum Group ("The Radium Girls"), NPR ("Dark Lives Of 'The Radium Girls' Left A Bright Legacy", 2017), Connecticut History
#Shorts #radiumgirls #history #darkhistory #mystery

entry.title: The night a quiet lake killed a valley 🌫️

media:group.media:title: The night a quiet lake killed a valley 🌫️
media:group.media:description:
Had you ever heard of Lake Nyos? 👇
On August 21, 1986, Lake Nyos in Cameroon released a cloud of carbon dioxide that killed 1,746 people and over 3,000 animals in one night. Scientists call it a limnic eruption.
Sources: Britannica, Eos (AGU), Penn State EARTH 105
#Shorts #lakenyos #darkhistory #history #mystery

entry.title: Kodak invented the thing that killed Kodak 📷

media:group.media:title: Kodak invented the thing that killed Kodak 📷
media:group.media:description:
Would you have bet against film in 1975? 👇
Kodak engineer Steve Sasson built the first digital camera in 1975. Kodak kept protecting its film business and filed for bankruptcy in 2012.
Sources: IEEE Spectrum ("The First Digital Camera"), PetaPixel (Sasson, 2010), Christian Science Monitor / AP (Kodak bankruptcy, Jan 19, 2012)
#Shorts #kodak #business #camera #entrepreneur #history
